item.text: {"question_id":"5B.8","answer":"In 2023, distributional policy combined targeted relief with materially unequal incidence. Sisi personally announced higher public-sector wages, a higher tax-exemption threshold, increased Takaful and Karama payments, and debt relief for some small farmers; the state programs were operationally administered through the Ministry of Social Solidarity, and by December Takaful and Karama reportedly reached 4.67 million households, with 74% of cardholders women. Its conditional and unconditional components targeted poor families, older people, orphans, widows, and people with disabilities, while the dynamic registry linked beneficiaries to other services. These records show policy choice and implementation mechanisms, but not that the measures were adequate or produced equal outcomes. Coverage remained disputed or incomplete: government-reported September coverage of more than 5 million families was about one-third of families living in or near poverty, and currency depreciation and inflation eroded transfer value. The announced wage and tax measures favored public-sector workers; private-sector and informal workers received weaker protection, private-sector real wages reportedly fell 33% over the preceding decade while public-sector wages rose about 9%, and the private-sector minimum lacked a binding enforcement mechanism. Social-pension spending was only 0.3% of GDP in 2023, while poor households faced disproportionate food-price exposure. Distribution was also regionally and socially unequal: poverty was substantially higher in parts of Upper Egypt; internet access was concentrated in Cairo and the Nile Delta; electricity cuts appeared longer in rural and impoverished areas; and women’s unemployment was reported at three times men’s. Agricultural and investment patterns under the Sisi administration privileged military, major national, foreign, and Gulf investors, while small farmers and agricultural workers remained marginalized. Carnegie further reports that military-managed projects diverted water from other cities, served affluent coastal or new-city consumers, could deprive small-scale farmers of water, displaced local communities and fishermen, and imposed opaque environmental burdens. Thus, the evidence supports real but targeted and partly implemented compensatory measures, alongside persistent class, labor-status, gender, regional, and community-level disparities; it does not establish fair actual incidence across all groups.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E005","BATCH-0022-E006","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0020-E013","BATCH-0020-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-R07-E010","BATCH-0009-R07-E011","BATCH-0022-E013","BATCH-0015-E009","BATCH-0021-E002","BATCH-0021-E003","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0002-E034","BATCH-0009-R11-E001","BATCH-0009-R11-E004","BATCH-0009-R10-E013","BATCH-0009-R10-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not provide a complete household-incidence study for 2023, beneficiary-level adequacy analysis, or a counterfactual welfare estimate.","Several favorable implementation figures are government- or program-reported and do not independently establish equal territorial performance, full funding, uptake, or improved living standards.","Some adverse findings describe national or longer-run conditions and do not isolate Sisi’s personal responsibility for every outcome;
